requirements: Start from the prior r3 disposable prototype only after verifying the archive hash. Reproduce and explain this source-level concern before changing it: its marked 503 exception survives as deepest cause when LBSolrClient exhausts endpoints; parallel CloudSolrClient.directUpdate wraps failed routes in RouteException, and sendRequest retryOn503 checks RouteException plus root 503 and can resend the whole batch. Establish actual behavior with a multi-shard test in which an atomic increment on one shard has completed before a second shard's marked rejection exhausts its alternatives. Check request counts, final persisted values and overall outcome. Do not claim a reproduction without execution.

Use a real multi-node multi-shard SolrCloud with at least one alternate suitable endpoint for a success leg: one shard has completed before another receives the genuine pre-handler shutdown rejection, and only the rejected subrequest is retried. Assert stored atomic increments and per-endpoint request counts. Repeat exhaustion with no viable alternate, covering the default parallel and sequential update paths and relevant delete-by-query/commit phase as feasible. No already-completed shard request may be resent; if the unchanged prototype fails, preserve fail-before evidence and try a bounded disposable correction. Re-run after any correction; distinguish pre-existing behavior from any new route triggered by the marker.

Assess repeatability beyond the prototype's getDocIterator guard: inspect supported request types, custom request writers and mutable or user-supplied request payloads. Exercise iterator and other concrete one-shot cases that exist, and fail closed unless repeatability is established. Test ordinary application 503 and missing marker; test body/stream closure on both clients, and explicitly account for marked-response handling in sync and async paths. If async is outside the proposed design, demonstrate it cannot accidentally enable unsafe replay and state the limitation.

Assess the marker's origin and intermediary trust: the prototype accepts any response with the header, so adding or forging it must not silently grant a safety guarantee. Exercise a header-adding/stripping intermediary or demonstrate and document a technically enforced direct-node boundary. Assess mixed-version unmarked servers. Verify a marker-emitting handler is actually loaded in a packaged distribution, not solely JettySolrRunner, or record the precise unresolved packaging gap.

Record actual source changes, commands, exit codes, fresh XML, logs, request counts and persisted values. Report success, failure or incomplete per leg; mock-only, setup failure or a single LB-only test does not prove multi-shard safety. The original in-flight indexing 503 remains unresolved unless separately demonstrated. Do not present the prototype as production ready without the named safety evidence. Publish the receipt before release with verified executor-stop evidence.
